risks.title: Commodity price volatility
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the document, mentioned at the outset of the risk factors. The language emphasizes 'high dependence' on corn, natural gas, and other commodity prices. Repetition and the magnitude of potential impacts (operating losses, production shutdowns) indicate an existential risk. The Macro category is heavily weighted here.

risks.title: Negative margin between costs and selling prices
risks.score_rationale: The document highlights that gross margin closely depends on the spread between ethanol, co-product prices, and corn. A negative or narrow spread is presented as potentially leading to operating losses. The risk is repeated multiple times with strong language ('sustained narrow or negative spread', 'adversely affect').

risks.title: Delays and failure of sequestration project
risks.score_rationale: The carbon sequestration project is tied to a $58.9 million investment, with permitting delays noted. The text mentions a 'significant write-off' and competitive disadvantage if the project fails. The new regulatory framework in Illinois (pipeline moratorium) increases regulatory risk.

risks.title: Increased competition and overcapacity
risks.score_rationale: The document notes national capacity of 18.5 billion gallons versus a regulatory mandate of 15 billion, creating excess capacity. The risk is described as potentially forcing price reductions below profitability thresholds. The tone is concerned but less alarming than for existential risks.

risks.title: Trade and tariff restrictions
risks.score_rationale: The risk relates to tariff threats from the Trump administration and potential retaliation from Canada and Mexico, key export markets. The text notes that 36% of ethanol exports go to Canada. The language is precautionary but highlights a possible 'material' impact.

risks.title: Decline in ethanol demand
risks.score_rationale: The document clearly raises the threat of electric vehicles and upcoming bans on internal combustion engines by 2035. Ethanol demand is highly dependent on gasoline consumption. The risk is presented as uncertain but high-impact, with mentions of federal legislation favoring electric vehicles.

risks.title: Inflation in production costs
risks.score_rationale: Inflation is mentioned as affecting materials, labor, and services. The text notes these increases may not be passed through to customers. While the language is less alarming than for other risks, the impact is described as 'negative' on results.
